label: Copy phase, outputting original token 2 (input = echoed token 1) in long sequences (L>=7)
explanation: Position feature for the copy phase. It fires at the step two after <DEL> (recall_idx == 2, prev2_tok == <DEL>), where the input is the echoed original token 1 and the model must output original token 2. Activation at recall_idx==2 grows with sequence length: firing rate is about 0.03 at L=6, around 0.5 at L=7, and most of the activation at L=8-9 (L>=8 alone gives precision 0.92). Top activations (~0.7-0.8) are all L=9. Which token is involved barely matters (lift for in_tok/out_tok is only 1.2-2.5x). Weak spillover onto the next step (recall_idx==3, about 3% of mass), mostly small values. It essentially does not fire in the original phase (0.6% of mass, small activations at t=1), at the delimiter, or later in the copy. It is silent at recall_idx==2 for short sequences (L<=5). Dev: recall_idx==2 alone gets recall 0.93 but precision 0.41; adding L>=7 gives P 0.79, R 0.89, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.94.

issues: Small factual error: the explanation says the firing rate at recall_idx==2 & L==6 is about 0.03. On test it is about 0.10 (precision 0.100 out of 82,766 steps), and the dev profile gives about 0.107 (8,940 active out of about 83k). It is still small, so the conclusion holds.

The 'L>=7' in the label is a soft boundary. On test, firing at recall_idx==2 is graded by length: L==7 has precision 0.52, L==8 has 0.86 and L==9 has 0.98. So only about half of L=7 sequences fire. L==9 alone holds 49% of the activation mass and L>=8 holds 80%.

No systematic split decides which L=7 sequences fire. At L=7, n_digits, digit vs letter in_tok/out_tok, a digit first token, and repeated tokens all leave precision in the 0.46-0.56 range. The L=7 false positives look like a diffuse threshold effect.

The other claims check out: 96.3% of the mass is at recall_idx==2, about 2.9% at recall_idx==3, 0.6% in the original phase (all at t=1), none at the delimiter, and L<=5 is nearly silent (precision 0.003). On test, recall_idx==2 & L>=7 gives precision 0.790, recall 0.891, F1 0.837 and mass recall 0.94, and L>=8 gives precision 0.92. The test misses (6% of the mass) are the recall_idx==3 tail, L=6 and t=1, which matches the explanation.
